_comment: Shipped address labels are first-party disclosed only: an exchange's own proof-of-reserves wallet list, a protocol's own deployment docs, or the exploited protocol's own incident report. Those live in disclosed-labels.json, which scripts/sync-disclosed-labels.mjs regenerates from the source documents and which records each entry's entity, evidence kind, source_url and retrieved_at. This file holds only entries that need no document, such as the zero address. Nothing inferred, scraped from a third-party tracker or guessed belongs in either file; case-specific attribution goes in a local override file pointed to by SUI_LABELS_FILE (same shape) or in manage_labels. Categories cex|bridge|mixer|malicious|burn terminate fund tracing as sinks. Keys may be a bare Sui address, which applies on every Sui network, or a CAIP-10 account id ('eip155:1:0x...') to scope an entry to one chain, which is how the far side of a bridge hop gets labeled.

0x00000000000000000000000000000000000000.label: Zero address
0x00000000000000000000000000000000000000.notes: Null/unset address; funds sent here are effectively burned or indicate an unset owner.
